# P1 + P2: no window in any space an unprivileged guest channel uses; Translated work in its own space

**STATUS: DESIGN-ONLY, revised 2026-10-04 after an adversarial security review and an adversarial
feasibility/regression review.** This text supersedes the 2026-10-03 P1+P2 design, its review, and the
2026-10-04 security-review revision (whose journaled copy is cut off mid-sentence; §14 records what each
review changed). Nothing in code has changed and no box has run.

- Verified at kayfabe `origin/master` `789dee9f`; `crates/kf-*` are unchanged since `e4fb0190`. Owner
  rulings §Q and §R are on master (`docs/OWNER_RULINGS.md:451-491`, `:493-…`).
- Ground truth: `research_clones/ogkm-580.159.04`. Closed GSP/firmware behaviour is marked **UNVERIFIED**.
- This document states properties and checks only. It does not describe misuse procedures.

## 0. The defect, restated so the fix is keyed to it

Every mirrored host VA space carries two read-write, non-privileged whole-object maps:
- the **store window**: all guest VRAM, including the guest kernel's GPU page tables and the firmware
  carve-out that holds kayfabe's declared BAR1/BAR2 roots (`kf-chip/src/bar0.rs:376-425`; `carve` at
  `:397`, roots at `:424-425`);
- the **guest-RAM window**: all guest RAM.

They are placed in three paths: `create_mirror` (`kf-qemu/src/mem.rs:1790`, `:1793`), `prewarm`
(`:1915`, `:1921`) and recycled spares (`:2150-2190`). `map_window` adds only `GROWS_DOWN` and, like every
kayfabe map, `CACHE_SNOOP` (`kf-host/src/channel.rs:377-390`, `kf-host/src/lib.rs:229-238`). Passthrough
twins, including guest user processes' channels, are born in the same space (`chan.rs:2831`).

MEASURED: guest-USER twins (`privilege=0`) were born in spaces logged with both windows
(`traces/v3_display/gop_box_20261003/run_b3_qemu.log:2747`, `:2803`). Only the Translated rewriter uses
window addresses (`chan.rs:492-524`, used at `:3380`); passthrough is unparsed. The windows are therefore
surplus to passthrough. This is audit S1-21, critical under §Q.

Two related gaps are closed by the same work:
- **S1-23.** The Translated rings sit in the guest kernel's mirror, and virtual operands and semaphores
  reach the engine unchanged (`translated.rs:26`, `:610-613`, `:677-679`).
- **The carve-out through the guest's own tables.** One `VaManager` bounds every vidmem/SKED leaf by
  `fb_length`, not `carve` (`device.rs:744-746`; `kf-mem/src/apply.rs:406`, `:596`). So a guest leaf into
  `[carve, fb_len)` is mapped, in twins as well. §Q says a passthrough space maps "no kayfabe memory".

## 1. The invariant, keyed on channel privilege

### 1.1 Where privilege comes from, and that it is known at the alloc

- The drainer decodes `ChannelPrivilege` from the alloc's `internalFlags` (`kf-rm/src/chanlink.rs:655`). It
  classifies the channel with `kernel_channel` (`:1378-1383`): kernel iff `PRIVILEGE == KERNEL`, or the
  client is in the RM-internal handle range (`:1362`).
- Guest userspace cannot set either. Guest CPU-RM recomputes the level from the call's security context
  (`ogkm kernel_channel.c:220`, `:274-291`). A userspace ioctl is `USER` or `USER_ROOT`, never `KERNEL`
  (`escape.c:304`). The level reaches the GSP (kayfabe) in the RPC's `internalFlags` (`:2803-2813`).
  Internal client handles start at `0xC1E00000`; user clients start at `0xC1D00000`
  (`resserv.h:135`, `:138`).
- The route split already turns on this (`passthrough = !a.kernel_client`, `chan.rs:2676`), at the
  alloc, before any work runs.

### 1.2 The invariant (a new `THE_CONSTRAINTS` section)

> A host VA space in which **any** channel the guest created non-kernel runs holds only rows derived from
> the guest's own page tables, placed FIXED at the guest's own VAs, at **user** privilege. None of those
> rows names the firmware carve-out. It holds no window and nothing kayfabe owns. The one space that holds
> the windows is kayfabe's per-VM Translated space (the **T-space**). Only kayfabe-authored work runs
> there, and every address that work dereferences is computed by kayfabe.

"At user privilege" is load-bearing. Host RM places its own privileged GR context buffers in the host hole
of any twin with a GR channel (`kf-host/src/channel.rs:57-97`). Only the PRIV PTE bit keeps a USER channel
off them, so this half depends on P0 (§9).

### 1.3 What P1 asserts by itself, and what it inherits

- P1 by itself: no window and no ring in any twin; a twin's guest leaves bounded by `carve` (§4.3); the
  mirror record separated from the windows.
- Inherited from P0 (`v3-sec-nonpriv`): twin channels **and T channels** are born USER (bit 5 clear), so
  `DENY_PHYSICAL_MODE_CE` (`kf-host/src/channel.rs:604-610`) and the PRIV PTE bit take effect (S1-20).

## 2. The T-space

### 2.1 What it maps, and nothing else

The T-space is one `FERMI_VASPACE_A` per kf3 device, built from objects kayfabe owns. It is allocated with
a new `alloc_vaspace_bare`, which makes none of the `GUEST_VA_RANGES` reservations (`channel.rs:180-238`),
because no guest row ever lands in it.

| region | contents | mapping | placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| ring region | `[RING_REGION_BASE, 2^40)` (`mem.rs:516`) | reserved first (`reserve_va`, `channel.rs:240-260`); rings are mapped FIXED through the reservation | fixed |
| store window | guest VRAM `[0, carve)`, including a preserved console region `[0, console)` (`bar0.rs:476-520`); **excludes** `[carve, fb_len)` | RW, `CACHE_SNOOP` | **bottom-up** (`high = false`), base read back |
| guest-RAM window | the whole guest memfd OS-descriptor object (`guest_ram_object`, `mem.rs:1657`) | RW, `CACHE_SNOOP`, GPU-uncached (§13) | bottom-up, first fit after the store window, base read back |

Nothing else is mapped. In particular there are no guest rows, no USERD, and no kernel CPU mapping on any
map (the `KERNEL_MAPPING` pin in `nvos46_map_flags` on `v3-dispsw-exp` covers T-space maps too).

### 2.2 Why every T-space address sits below 2^40, on every family

- The **legacy host semaphore** `SEMAPHOREA/B` is 40-bit on every family (`cl906f.h:79`, `clc46f.h:77`,
  `clc56f.h:77`). Stock CeUtils releases its PB-get index with it **on every family**
  (`channelAddHostSema`, `channel_utils.c:731-746`, called at `:849`, `:986`).
- `SEM_ADDR_HI` is 40-bit on Turing–Ada (`clc46f.h:204`, `clc56f.h:209`) and 57-bit from Hopper
  (`clc86f.h:145`, `clc96f.h:78`, `clca6f.h:39`).
- A GP entry's address is 40-bit on every family (`kf-chan/src/host.rs:24-30`).

So both windows and the ring region must lie below 2^40. **`GROWS_DOWN` is forbidden in the T-space.** RM
placed a `GROWS_DOWN` window at `0x1fffe00000000` (`run_b3_qemu.log:2747`). With that placement every
CeUtils PB-get release would be truncated, and `RmInitAdapter` would fail on every family. Bottom-up first
fit is MEASURED at `fb_base=0x120000000`, `ram_base=0x405200000`, 306 ms total on GA106/580
(`THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md:718-736`).

The T-space build refuses by name if either window ends above `RING_REGION_BASE`. That bounds guest RAM +
FB to about 1 TiB − 4.5 GiB − 4 GiB. A per-operand check at `≥ 2^40` stays as a second bound (§3.4).

### 2.3 Built once, at prewarm, never lazily

- **Order:** `alloc_vaspace_bare`, then reserve the ring region, map the store window, map the RAM window,
  check both ends, and record the result. This is the first thing `prewarm` does, on its first tick, which
  already pins the RAM object (`mem.rs:1894-1956`; called at `device.rs:1534-1550`, as soon as QEMU
  registers guest RAM and long before the guest driver loads).
- **Cost:** paid once per VM, not per mirror. Store window ~1 ms (`THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md` §14). RAM
  window 65–86 ms on one box (`mem.rs:961-966`, w827) and 672–906 ms in the app-matrix run
  (`traces/v3_cdp/app_matrix_2830988f`, per the S1-21 verification).
- **Never lazily.** A Translated birth before the T-space exists is refused by name: `tspace: not built
  (<why>)`. There is no fallback to mirror windows, because a fallback would reopen S1-21. Building on the
  birth path would put the pin and map inside a held reply on the single act thread (`chan.rs:1263-1278`).
  The first-mirror cold cost was measured at 7.6 s against a 6 s GSP RPC timeout (`mem.rs` `create_mirror`
  doc, pr1).
- **The T-space requires the RAM object.** CeUtils and UVM semaphores and pushbuffers are in sysmem
  (`THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md:419-420`). With no RAM window, the build refuses by name.
- **Gate:** the box log shows the `tspace …` line before the first `BORN Translated` line.

### 2.4 The rings

Each Translated ring is born in the T-space at a T-space ring slot. The ring keeps **one** 1 MiB
device-local object and **one** CPU view: a separate object per region would add host BAR1 views per ring,
and BAR1 exhaustion is the v3-appfix J regression (`host.rs:85-92`). The ring is re-laid-out so that every
region is whole 64 KiB granules. Each map is then big-page-congruent, so `nvos46_page_size_flag` keeps big
pages (`kf-abi/src/bringup.rs:913-924`) and no 4 KiB sub-mapping question arises.

| range | offset | length | GPU mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| pushbuffer | `0x0` | `0xD_0000` (832 KiB) | read-only |
| GPFIFO | `0xD_0000` | `0x1_0000` (512 entries use 4 KiB) | read-only |
| fence | `0xE_0000` | `0x1_0000` | read-write |
| USERD | `0xF_0000` | `0x1_0000` | **not mapped** |

- PBDMA reaches USERD through the instance block (`RingSpec{userd_memory, userd_offset}`,
  `host.rs:222-228`), and kayfabe writes `GP_PUT` through its CPU view, so USERD needs no GPU mapping.
- §Q requires the read-only maps: "mapped read-only except its fence". The **mechanism** that keeps guest
  work off the ring is authorship (§3): no emitted address can land in the ring region, because every
  emitted address is a window address bounded by the window's length. The read-only maps are the second
  bound.
- The half-pushbuffer limit becomes 416 KiB (`push_inner`, `host.rs:343-347`). §3.5's chunk cap keeps every
  piece far below it.
- **Ring slots become per-VM:** 4096 slots (`mem.rs:516-547`) shared by all Translated channels for the
  VM's life. Today a slot is returned only on a fully successful release (`give_ring_slot`, `:549`); in
  the T-space a refused release leaks the slot until the VM ends. This is counted, the count is gated
  (§8), and exhaustion is refused by name, as today.
- Read-only GPU maps of guest leaves are already placed by v3-roperm (`MapPerm`,
  `channel.rs:1107-1135`). PBDMA fetching through a read-only map is **UNVERIFIED**; T-TSPACE-BUILD checks it.

### 2.5 Isolation by type, and the client

- `TSpace` is a distinct type. `birth_twin_in` cannot accept it, it is never inserted into `Mirrors`, and
  only `TSpace::ring()` places a map in it.
- For now the T-space is built in C1. OWNER_RULINGS §N says kayfabe's own allocations live outside the
  client whose display-SW address check is client-wide (`V3_DISPLAY.md` on `v3-dispsw-exp`, true-bound item
  1). Host RM writes a display-SW release only through a kernel CPU mapping, and no kayfabe map carries one
  (the `KERNEL_MAPPING` pin), so the T-space adds no write path. The move to client K happens with the §N
  client split. That split is already a precondition of x11-dispsw default-on, so P1+P2 does not wait on it.
  Duplicating the store and RAM objects into K is allowed by source (`sharing.c:345-352`) and **UNVERIFIED**.

### 2.6 The vIOMMU seam (§Q fourth address kind)

- A single function, `dma_to_file_range(dma, len)`, is the only path from a device DMA address to a memfd
  range. Every resolver uses it:
  - walker sysmem leaves (the `VaManager` `ram_offset` closure, `device.rs:744-747`);
  - `SlotWindow`'s sysmem arm (`chan.rs:514-520`);
  - sysmem USERD and notifiers.
- Today it is `RamMap::file_range`. Under a vIOMMU it does IOVA→GPA per run first, splitting a run where
  the mapping is discontiguous and refusing (never reading through) an unmapped run (`V3_VIOMMU.md` §3).
- The T-space RAM window is never unmapped on a guest vIOMMU invalidation. The sync point for T channels is
  therefore: every piece bound under the old translation has **completed** (its fence) before the guest's
  invalidation completes. This has the same shape as `V3_VIOMMU.md` §3 item 3.
- Until this is built, kf3 refuses at realize behind a vIOMMU. That is unchanged.

## 3. The rewriter as an address author

Today the rewriter (`kf-chan/src/translated.rs`) rewrites physical CE operands and forwards everything
else as written: host methods below `0x100` (`:610-613`), the CE default arm (`:677-679`), the
`SubDeviceMask` header raw (`:453-457`), `SET_OBJECT` with the guest's full word (`:525-540`), MEMBAR/L2
`MEM_OP` A–C as written (`:563-599`), and the `LAUNCH_DMA` word minus two bits (`:836`). Under T-mode,
every word kayfabe emits is authored from decoded, validated fields.

### 3.1 The property

- On a T channel, every address the engine dereferences is computed by kayfabe. It lies inside
  `[fb_base, fb_base+carve)` or `[ram_base, ram_base+ram_len)`.
- No guest-written address value is ever emitted.
- Every emitted `(subchannel, method)` is in the per-tier allowlist, or is an authored address register.
- No guest word is copied. Each emitted word is built from decoded fields that passed the tier's field
  table.

### 3.2 What is authored, by method class

- **Address registers are state, never output:** CE `OFFSET_IN/OUT_UPPER/LOWER`, `SET_SEMAPHORE_A/B`,
  `SET_MONITORED_FENCE_SIGNAL_ADDR_*`; host `SEMAPHOREA/B`, `SEM_ADDR_LO/HI`.
- **Footprint registers are state, re-emitted at each trigger:** `LINE_LENGTH_IN`, `LINE_COUNT`,
  `PITCH_IN/OUT`, `SET_REMAP_*`. The engine therefore always runs with exactly the values the bound was
  computed from. This replaces today's post-launch restore (`:838-845`).
- **`SET_*_PHYS_MODE` are state only.** No T launch is physical. `PEER` is refused (as today). A non-zero
  FLA, PEER_ID or BASIC_KIND field is refused by name where the tier defines one.
- **`SET_OBJECT`** is authored as the host ring's own CE class with `ENGINE = 0`. `GP100_UVM_SW` is consumed
  (as today). Any other class is refused (as today).
- **`LAUNCH_DMA`** is authored from a per-tier field table. The table must carry every field stock sets:
  - `SRC_TYPE` and `DST_TYPE` are always VIRTUAL; reserved bits are zero.
  - Forwarded field values:
    - `DISABLE_PLC` (UVM on C7B5, `uvm_ampere_ce.c:112-114`; CeUtils on C8B5, `channel_utils.c:684`);
    - `FLUSH_ENABLE/TYPE`;
    - `DATA_TRANSFER_TYPE` NONE, PIPELINED or NON_PIPELINED (`CAB5` `PREFETCH = 3` is gated on the census,
      `clcab5.h:29-41`);
    - `SEMAPHORE_TYPE` 0, 1 or 2;
    - the `SEMAPHORE_REDUCTION` fields;
    - `SEMAPHORE_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (C8B5+, `clc8b5.h:89`);
    - `INTERRUPT_TYPE` NONE or NON_BLOCKING (CeUtils sets NON_BLOCKING with a callback,
      `channel_utils.c:658-661`);
    - `REMAP_ENABLE`;
    - `MULTI_LINE_ENABLE`;
    - the memory layouts.
  - Refused by name:
    - `SEMAPHORE_TYPE == 3` (`clc7b5.h:101`);
    - `INTERRUPT_TYPE == BLOCKING` (no stock emitter found);
    - `VPRMODE ≠ 0` on C7B5;
    - `COPY_TYPE ≠ DEFAULT` on C8B5+ (`uvm_hopper_ce.c:195-213`).
  - The Hopper+ fast scrub is converted to a virtual remap fill, as today (`:776-808`).
  - A non-zero field the table does not name is counted by the shadow (§3.6), then refused per tier.
    It is **never silently cleared**, because a dropped field changes behaviour without a refusal.
- **`MEM_OP`:**
  - `TLB_INVALIDATE` stays a split (`:573-591`).
  - MEMBAR and L2 operations are authored from the decoded operation and its type fields (`MEMBAR_TYPE`,
    the L2 op), never from the guest's A–C words.
  - `ACCESS_COUNTER_CLR` is served (as today).
  - Anything else is refused (as today).
- **Address-free host methods are authored with their argument:** NOP with inline payload, WFI,
  `NON_STALL_INTERRUPT`, `SET_REFERENCE`, `YIELD`, `FB_FLUSH`. Each is census-confirmed per tier.
- **Hopper+ `SET_MEMORY_SCRUB_PARAMETERS` (0x6FC) is address-free.** Stock pushes it
  (`channel_utils.c:675-676`, `uvm_hopper_ce.c:251`); refusing it would break Hopper and Blackwell.
- **Refused by name, on every tier:**
  - host `CLEAR_FAULTED` (0x84). UVM pushes it only while servicing non-replayable faults
    (`uvm_turing_host.c:73-92`), and kayfabe delivers none;
  - CE `SET_MONITORED_FENCE_TYPE` and `_SIGNAL_ADDR_*` (0x21C–0x224);
  - `SET_RENDER_ENABLE_A/B/C` (0x254–0x25C);
  - `PM_TRIGGER` (0x140) and `PM_TRIGGER_END`;
  - `SET_SECURE_COPY_MODE` (0x500) and the Hopper confidential-computing address methods (0x514–0x53C,
    `clc8b5.h:100-115`; stock uses them only under confidential computing, `uvm_hopper_ce.c:545`, `:588`).

### 3.3 Triggers

Each of these is a trigger:
- a CE `LAUNCH_DMA` that moves data, releases a semaphore, or both;
- **every** host `SEMAPHORED` operation (RELEASE, ACQUIRE, ACQ_GEQ, ACQ_AND, REDUCTION);
- **every** host `SEM_EXECUTE` operation, including the acquire forms UVM uses (`ACQ_CIRC_GEQ` with
  `ACQUIRE_SWITCH_TSG`, `uvm_turing_host.c:53-70`, `uvm_hopper_host.c:55-73`) and `RELEASE_TIMESTAMP`
  (`:75-95`).

An unknown operation is refused by name. At each trigger the rewriter resolves the operands (§3.4), checks
them, and emits the authored address registers, the footprint registers and the trigger word.

### 3.4 Translation, by operand kind

- **Physical operand:** today's arithmetic. A `LocalFb` operand is bounded to `[0, carve)`, not `fb_len`
  (`Windows::translate`, `chan.rs:497`). A sysmem operand goes through `dma_to_file_range` and the RAM
  window (`:514-520`).
- **Virtual operand or semaphore:** resolved through the placement rows of the guest VA space the channel
  was born in (`PlacedRows`, `mem.rs:479`; `resolve_placed_prefix`, `:495`), **under one read guard per
  operand**. Adjacent rows that are contiguous in both VA and backing are merged. Each piece becomes
  `fb_base+off` or `ram_base+off`. A piece that resolves into `[carve, fb_len)` is refused.
- **Extents:** data uses `extents()` (`translated.rs:687-724`). A semaphore uses 4 bytes, or 8 with a 64-bit
  payload (C8B5 `SEMAPHORE_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, host `SEM_EXECUTE PAYLOAD_SIZE`), or 16 for a four-word or
  timestamped release. A semaphore must lie inside one row, or it is refused.
- **Permissions:** `PlacedRows` gains a `MapPerm` field. Today a row is `va → (len, off, ram)`; it carries the
  guest leaf's permission (`Desired.perm`, `apply.rs:36-40`). A write, release or reduction through a
  read-only row is refused by name, and so is a reduction through an `atomic_disable` row.
- **Discontiguous operands:**
  - A 1-D operand is split at the union of the source and destination row boundaries. A boundary inside a
    remap element is refused.
  - The first piece keeps the guest's `DATA_TRANSFER_TYPE`. The **last** piece is `NON_PIPELINED` and alone
    carries the semaphore, interrupt and flush.
  - A multi-line operand must be contiguous over its whole pitch footprint, or it is refused.
  - A block-linear virtual operand is refused, because `extents` ignores layout.
  - Stock UVM never sets `MULTI_LINE` (`uvm_volta_ce.c:168`, `:246`; `uvm_hopper_ce.c:278`, `:476`). Its
    virtual operands are inline data (≤ 8 KiB, `uvm_push.c:446`), semaphores, and one-page CPU staging
    (`uvm_va_block.c:13065`, `:13172`).
- **Bounds:**
  - at most 64 pieces per launch, refused by name past that (R2.4);
  - a host semaphore that resolves at or above 2^40 on a 40-bit form is refused (§2.2).
- **Row exactness is a safety property now.** `unmap_range` removes only rows whose **start** lies in the
  range (`mem.rs:842-850`). Host RM splits a straddling placement and keeps its outside part
  (`channel.rs:405-407`). Two consequences:
  - A row that straddles the start stays recorded at full length: stale coverage, an A.9 concern.
  - A row that starts inside the range but extends past its end is dropped whole while host RM keeps the
    outside part: missing coverage, which is a false refusal that kills the channel.

  Fix: trim or split at both edges, exactly as host RM does, with a test for each edge.

### 3.5 Bind at submit, and chunking

- Today `ring.rs:216` rewrites a whole segment at fetch and holds the decoded words. Under T-mode the
  rewriter emits an unbound IR: `Raw(words)`, `CeLaunch{regs, launch}`, `HostSem{regs, op}` and
  `Invalidate{pdb}`.
- The pump binds each piece **when it pushes it** (inside `TranslatedChannel::pump`, `host.rs:722-740`).
  That is after any earlier split's walk has completed (`:698-711`). A piece the host ring refuses as
  `Busy` is stashed **unbound**.
- **Chunking:** the IR is cut into pieces at trigger boundaries, with a cap of 64 KiB per piece. T-mode
  re-emits ~10–14 authored words per trigger, so a launch-dense segment can expand ~3.5× over its
  256 KiB input (`ring.rs:20`). An unchunked piece could exceed the half-pushbuffer limit, which is a
  channel-killing error (`host.rs:343-347`). Ordering inside one channel is unchanged.
- **Guarantees:** an operand bound after the guest's last invalidate on its own channel sees the
  post-invalidate rows. That is legal stale-TLB behaviour within one channel.
- **Not guaranteed:** translation at execution time across channels. A piece pushed behind a host acquire
  is bound before another channel's walk could complete. Stock producers appear safe: UVM waits on its
  kernel-mapping PTE writes on the CPU (`uvm_tracker_wait_deinit`), and CeUtils' `pbGpuVA` is fixed. This is
  **UNVERIFIED**. A stale-bind counter (§7.13) re-resolves each bound piece when its fence retires and
  counts mismatches. If it is ever non-zero, a host acquire becomes a bind barrier. Reach stays within
  guest memory either way.

### 3.6 Classification tables, the census, and the shadow

- The allowlist **cannot be generated from headers.** `clc9b5.h` defines only the class id; `clcab5.h`
  defines two methods (`LAUNCH_DMA` 0x300, `REQ_ATTR` 0x754); `clc86f.h` and `clc96f.h` list no
  `SEMAPHOREA-D`, `NOP` or `NON_STALL_INTERRUPT`. Yet CeUtils pushes `NV906F_SEMAPHOREA-D` on every family,
  and UVM inherits CE bodies by `parent_id` (`uvm_hal.c:143-180`: C7B5 → C8B5 → C9B5 → CAB5).
- **The tables are per tier and per offset.** They are written by hand, classified by semantics, and each
  row names the class it inherits from. Each row has one of three dispositions: address (§3.4),
  address-free (authored, §3.2), or refused by name. Field tables cover `LAUNCH_DMA`, the `SEMAPHORED` and
  `SEM_EXECUTE` operations, and `MEM_OP_D`.
- **The census is a dedicated, count-only instrument.** It is not `KF3_COMPLETION_PROBE`, which keeps 4 and
  drops the rest (`translated.rs:180-307`). It counts per `(tier, subchannel kind, method)`, records the set
  of `LAUNCH_DMA` field values seen, the operation values, the header forms and the GP-entry opcodes, and
  dumps one line per channel at free.
- **The shadow.** Before any behaviour change, the T-mode rewriter and resolver run **in shadow** on today's
  path behind `KF3_TSHADOW=1`. They compute what T-mode would emit and discard it, counting:
  - `would_refuse` by reason;
  - resolution misses, including a miss that only a withheld privileged leaf would have covered;
  - pieces per launch (maximum);
  - unknown fields;
  - unclassified pairs.

  The shadow measures both the method census and resolution coverage with no risk. Precedent: the live
  walk shadow (`compared=65 disagreements=0`).
- **Hardware coverage is uneven.** The families measured on hardware are TU116, GA106/GA104, AD106/AD104
  and GB203/GB205 (`docs/STATUS_DETAIL.md:54-59`, `:297-308`). Hopper, GA100 and GB10x are source-only.
  GB20x's census exercises the C8B5-inherited CE body and the Hopper-derived host body, which covers most
  of the Hopper tier.
- **S1-21 is not gated on the census** (§8). Window removal depends only on the T-space and the resolver.
  The census gates refusal of *unclassified* methods (S1-23), per family.

### 3.7 Header forms
design_issues: [HIGH] Window placement contradicts the 40-bit host-semaphore requirement. The design's T-space table maps the store window with map_window(..., high=true), i.e. GROWS_DOWN (kf-host channel.rs:377-390). RM then places it at the top of the space: measured at 0x1fffe00000000 (run_b3_qemu.log:2747; THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md:1056). But §2.2 requires windows below 2^40, because SEM_ADDR_HI is 7:0 on Turing-Ada (clc46f.h:204, clc56f.h:209). With GROWS_DOWN every rewritten host semaphore fails the limit, including CeUtils' channelAddHostSema release on every family (channel_utils.c:719, called at :849 and :986), so RmInitAdapter would fail on Turing-Ada. Fix: in the T-space, place windows bottom-up (high=false, matching the §15/§17 measurement at 0x120000000). Reserve the ring region first. Refuse by name any window that ends past RING_REGION_BASE. Add a unit test that fails if GROWS_DOWN is passed.

[HIGH] Partial re-authoring leaves guest words on the wire. Today the rewriter copies the LAUNCH_DMA word minus two bits (translated.rs:836), forwards SET_OBJECT with the guest's full word, ENGINE field included (:527-531), forwards SET_*_PHYS_MODE (:642-643, then emit at :677), forwards header forms verbatim (:453-455), and forwards MEM_OP A-C as written for MEMBAR/L2 (:567, :594). The design classifies these as 'address-free, forwarded'. Fix: in T-mode no guest word is copied. Every emitted word is authored from decoded, validated fields: LAUNCH_DMA from a per-tier field allowlist with both TYPE bits always VIRTUAL and reserved bits zero; SET_OBJECT as the host ring's own CE class with ENGINE=0; PHYS_MODE consumed as state, with FLA/PEER_ID/BASIC_KIND≠0 refused; footprint registers re-emitted from CeState at each trigger, so the engine always runs with exactly the values the bound was computed from.

[MEDIUM-HIGH] The trigger set is incomplete. Every host SEMAPHORED operation (ACQUIRE, ACQ_GEQ, ACQ_AND, REDUCTION, as well as RELEASE) and every SEM_EXECUTE operation dereferences the address registers (clc46f.h/clc56f.h enums). The design names only 'SEMAPHORED release'. Fix: every SEMAPHORED and SEM_EXECUTE operation is a trigger. Unknown operations are refused. Extents come from RELEASE_SIZE, PAYLOAD_SIZE and RELEASE_TIMESTAMP.

[MEDIUM] Stock-required and newer methods are missing from the classification. SET_MEMORY_SCRUB_PARAMETERS (0x6FC, C8B5+) is pushed by stock CeUtils and UVM (channel_utils.c:676; uvm_hopper_ce.c:251), so refusing it breaks Hopper/Blackwell. SET_SECURE_COPY_MODE (0x500) is not classified. CAB5 adds DATA_TRANSFER_TYPE_PREFETCH (3) and REQ_ATTR (0x754) (clcab5.h). LAUNCH_DMA INTERRUPT_TYPE BLOCKING has no disposition. The census must also be keyed on field values (for LAUNCH_DMA, SEMAPHORED, SEM_EXECUTE and MEM_OP_D operations), not only on (family, method).

[MEDIUM] Header forms that change which later methods execute (the subdevice-mask forms) are forwarded as written today. In T-mode they must either be refused by name (census-gated; a single-GPU guest has no use for them) or be proven unable to separate an authored address write from its trigger or from the completion tail. Add it as a named refusal and a property test.

[MEDIUM] GP control entries are silently skipped (ring.rs:194; gp_entry_decode returns None for LENGTH==0, kf-abi submit.rs:1974). This includes Hopper/Blackwell UVM's SET_PB_SEGMENT_EXTENDED_BASE (uvm_hopper_host.c:419-425), so later segments are read at the wrong VA. The design proposes scoping the matrix to Turing-Ada, which conflicts with ruling A.7 (all families first-class). Fix in increment A: decode the extended base, and refuse every other control opcode by name.

[MEDIUM] In T-mode PlacedRows becomes the GPU's translation, so its exactness is now a safety property. unmap_range removes only rows whose start lies inside the range (mem.rs:840-846), so a row that straddles the range start keeps its full length. Fix: split or trim straddling rows, resolve each operand under a single read guard, and add a partial-unmap test. Under owner ruling §R(b) the resolver and the address emitter are perimeter material.

[MEDIUM] The design does not apply §R. Bound checks are spread across translate, extents and the host-semaphore path. Fix: one perimeter file (kf-chan tspace_unsafe.rs) holding the window bounds ([0,carve), RAM length, host-semaphore limit), an opaque address type that only this file can construct, and the only functions that put an address word or a LAUNCH_DMA word into the output. List them in the §R gate-3 export table, with the tests that show each check.

[MEDIUM] Splitting is unbounded. A virtual operand is split per discontiguous row, so one guest launch can expand into an unbounded number of pieces and unbounded memory. This violates R2.4. Fix: a per-launch piece bound and a per-segment output bound, each refused by name, with a test.

[MEDIUM] Isolation of the T-space by type and by client. Nothing in the design structurally stops a passthrough birth from targeting the T-space. Fix: TSpace is a distinct type that birth_twin_in cannot accept, and it is never inserted into Mirrors. §N notes the display-SW address check is client-wide (V3_DISPLAY.md on v3-dispsw-exp :305-311), and which hVASpace GSP names there is closed firmware. [MEDIUM] The mixing/flip state machine as written holds a lock across walker host ioctls, which conflicts with A.4. Fix: one atomic per-twin word {Unclassified|User(n)|Kernel} with CAS transitions. Kernel is sticky until retire. Unclassified withholds privileged leaves. Passthrough births are refused (never waited on) while the state is Kernel. Add a forced-interleaving test. T births still count in mirror.live, so a mirror under a live T channel is never recycled.

[MEDIUM] The ring layout depends on page size. Sub-range maps of a single ring object could carry a large PTE over USERD. Fix by construction: USERD in its own object, never GPU-mapped; pushbuffer and GPFIFO in one object mapped read-only; the fence in its own object mapped read-write. Whether host RM accepts a read-only GPFIFO mapping is UNVERIFIED and is checked in T-TSPACE-BUILD.

[HIGH] Windows placed with GROWS_DOWN break RmInitAdapter on every family, not only Turing-Ada. CeUtils releases its PB-get index with the legacy NV906F SEMAPHOREA on every family (channel_utils.c:731-746, called at :849 and :986). SEMAPHOREA_OFFSET_UPPER is 7:0, so the address is 40-bit (cl906f.h:79, clc46f.h:77, clc56f.h:77). A GROWS_DOWN window lands at 0x1fffe00000000 (run_b3_qemu.log:2747), so every rewritten host release would be truncated. Fix: build the T-space as a bare space. Reserve [RING_REGION_BASE, 2^40) first with reserve_va (channel.rs:240-260). Map both windows bottom-up (measured 0x120000000 and 0x405200000, 306 ms, THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md:718-736). Refuse by name if either window ends past RING_REGION_BASE. Add a unit test that fails if the builder passes GROWS_DOWN.

[HIGH] Closing S1-21 does not have to wait for the per-family method census. Removing the windows depends only on the T-space plus the address resolver. The census gates only the refusal of unclassified methods (S1-23). Hardware also bounds what a census can cover: only TU116, GA106/GA104, AD106/AD104 and GB203/GB205 exist on hardware. Hopper, GA100 and GB10x are source-only (docs/STATUS_DETAIL.md:54-59, :297-308), so a census-gated P1 could never close S1-21 there. Fix: S1-21 closes at default-on (inc E) on every family. Unclassified-method refusal turns on per family as each census lands (owner decision 2).

[HIGH] There is no zero-risk step before behaviour changes. Fix: in inc C, run the T-mode rewriter and resolver in shadow on today's path behind KF3_TSHADOW=1, count-only. It counts: would-refuse by reason; resolution misses, including those only a withheld privileged leaf would have covered; pieces per launch; unknown LAUNCH_DMA fields; unclassified (subch, method) pairs; header forms; GP opcodes. One shadow run per measured family yields both the census and resolution coverage. Default-on is gated on those counters being 0. Precedent: the live walk shadow (compared=65 disagreements=0).

[HIGH] Authoring every LAUNCH_DMA word drops stock bits unless each tier's field table is complete. Examples: UVM sets DISABLE_PLC on C7B5 (uvm_ampere_ce.c:112-114) and CeUtils on C8B5 (channel_utils.c:684); FLUSH_TYPE GL/SYS; the SEMAPHORE_REDUCTION fields (uvm_volta_ce.c:88-94); SEMAPHORE_PAYLOAD_SIZE 27:27 on C8B5 (clc8b5.h:89); INTERRUPT_TYPE NON_BLOCKING (channel_utils.c:658-661); DATA_TRANSFER_TYPE PREFETCH on CAB5 (clcab5.h:29-41). Semaphore extents must include 64-bit payloads (8 B) and timestamps (16 B). INTERRUPT_TYPE BLOCKING is refused (no stock emitter).

[MEDIUM-HIGH] Expanded T-mode output can exceed the host pushbuffer's half-size limit. push_inner returns a channel-killing error for any piece over PB_BYTES/2 (host.rs:343-347). T-mode re-emits about 10-14 authored words per trigger, so a launch-dense segment can grow ~3.5x over the 256 KiB maximum input (ring.rs:20). Fix: chunk the IR at trigger boundaries with a fixed 64 KiB cap per piece. Add a unit test with a maximum-size, launch-dense segment.

[MEDIUM-HIGH] PlacedRows can be wrong at both edges of an unmap, not only the start. unmap_range removes only rows whose start lies in the range (mem.rs:842-850), but host RM splits a straddling placement and keeps its outside part (channel.rs:405-407). A row that straddles the start leaves stale coverage (an A.9 concern). A row that starts inside the range and runs past its end is dropped whole while the host keeps its tail: missing coverage, so a valid T operand is refused and the UVM channel dies. Under T-mode this is a regression, not just a hazard. Fix: trim or split at both edges, matching the host. Test each edge.

[MEDIUM] The ring layout should avoid both the page-size question and an increase in host BAR1 use. Separate objects per region would each need a CPU view, which reintroduces the v3-appfix J host-BAR1 exhaustion (host.rs:85-92). The second security pass said sub-range maps would be "refused"; that is overstated, because nvos46_page_size_flag already falls back to 4 KiB (bringup.rs:913-924, lib.rs:1108-1135). Fix: keep one object and one CPU view, and re-lay the ring in whole 64 KiB granules: pushbuffer 0x0-0xD0000 read-only, GPFIFO 0xD0000 read-only, fence 0xE0000 read-write, USERD 0xF0000 not mapped. Every map is then big-page-congruent. §Q requires the read-only maps; authorship is the mechanism that keeps work off the ring.

[MEDIUM] Routing operands through the RAM window changes their cache attribute. Today a virtual sysmem operand goes through a mirror row placed with the guest leaf's volatile bit (MapPerm, channel.rs:1107-1135). Through the window it gets RM's default, so a CPU-written sysmem semaphore acquired by a T channel could be read from a stale GPU L2 line. Fix: map the T-space RAM window GPU-uncached (NVOS46_FLAGS_GPU_CACHEABLE_NO, bringup.rs:767). Check it with a CPU-written semaphore acquire in the T-RING-TRANSLATED module. UNVERIFIED.

[MEDIUM] Bounding every target by carve at once could break boot. One VaManager with store_bytes=fb_length serves the GPU mirrors and the BAR1/BAR2 CPU windows (device.rs:744-760); PRAMIN is bounded separately (mem.rs:1699-1711). CeUtils VIRTUAL_MODE maps an FB alias over [heap.base, heap.base+heap.total) (mem_utils_gm107.c:590-601). That mode is enabled by memory-config facts that kayfabe's GSP reports (mem_mgr.c:4130-4138), and whether the alias range includes the carve-out is unverified. A false refusal fails RmInitAdapter. Fix: give each target its own bound. GPU-mirror targets get the carve bound, count-only for one A/B run per measured family and then refused (S1-23 asks for exactly this). BAR1, BAR2 and PRAMIN CPU views stay count-only for a later decision. T-space translation and USERD/notifier get the bound now. The NVOS32_TYPE_RESERVED exception is RM's own bookkeeping block (heap.c:300-333), not a client placement.

[MEDIUM] The journal's recommended interim P1 (windows only in Kernel-classified spaces) has a measured cost. The windows would be mapped lazily at UVM's first Translated birth. The RAM-window map costs 65-86 ms on vh2 (mem.rs:961-966) and 672-906 ms in the app-matrix run (S1-21 verification, c10). It would run inside a held alloc reply on the single act thread (chan.rs:1263-1278), once per UVM VA space; that is per CUDA process in serial runs. Presented as owner decision 1 with that cost. Recommendation: no; go straight to the T-space with shadow-first staging.

[MEDIUM] Building the T-space has ordering and failure rules the design does not state. A Translated birth before the T-space exists must be refused by name, with no lazy build and no fallback to mirror windows (a fallback would reopen S1-21). The T-space must be built on prewarm's first tick, before any spare (device.rs:1534-1550). It requires the guest-RAM object, because CeUtils and UVM pushbuffers and semaphores are in sysmem. Gate: the tspace log line precedes the first BORN Translated line.

[MEDIUM] Ring slots become a per-VM pool and can leak for the VM's lifetime. The pool has 4096 slots (mem.rs:516-547). Today a slot returns only on a fully successful release (give_ring_slot, :549), and a leak dies with its mirror. In the T-space a leaked slot is lost until the VM ends. Fix: count leaks, and gate on slots-in-use returning to baseline after each process.

[MEDIUM] Hopper+ control GP entries are skipped, and the 403 draft's reason for flagging this was wrong. UVM writes SET_PB_SEGMENT_EXTENDED_BASE (uvm_channel.c:2536-2544, uvm_hopper_host.c:419-425). gp_entry_decode returns None for any zero-length entry (submit.rs:1979-1981), and the ring skips it (ring.rs:193-195). [MEDIUM] Under §R(b) the rewriter is already perimeter material, and the design does not move it. Today's put_offset emits window VAs, which hardware dereferences, from a safe file (translated.rs:750-753). The ring's own address authoring is the same: fence_words (host.rs:43-55) and the GP entry in push_inner (:369). That is §56.2's first option ("the guest's map call already told us"), but it changes the role §56 rule 2 governs (THE_CONSTRAINTS.md:3785-3820), so the owner should confirm it explicitly (decision 4). S1-60 (stale VER3 4 KiB translations) and S1-81 (late invalidate) apply to T operands exactly as they apply to mirrors: no new reach and no improvement.

findings.issue: This is a functional bug that breaks T-mode itself. With KF3_TSPACE=1, record_twin stores fb_len=0 to mean 'no store window'. The same field is also the bound on the CPU store views that Mem::read uses to fetch a Translated channel's GPFIFO entries and pushbuffer through vidmem rows. view_for computes len = VIEW_BYTES.min(0 - off) = 0 and returns 'store offset .. is past the store (0x0)'. Every vidmem GP fetch therefore fails with RingRefusal::Read and the channel dies. UVM's default GPFIFO location on a non-coherent dGPU is vidmem (uvm_channel.c:3386-3390), so every UVM Translated channel dies at its first fetch. On the default path the field is plane.fb_len (mem.rs:1973), which is why nothing shows today. The box-log gate would not name this failure: NO-DEAD-BIND only matches 'DEAD: tspace bind:'.
findings.fix: Do not overload Mirror::fb_len. Pass the store bound to StoreViews separately: plane.fb_len, or in T-mode the carve so CPU reads never touch the carve-out either. Alternatively give twins an explicit window: Option and keep a separate store_len. Add a kf-qemu unit test that reads a vidmem row through Mem for a T-mode twin, and widen the gate's dead-channel check to any 'DEAD:' on a Translated token.

findings.issue: The stale-bind instrument reports problems on correct runs and misses the case that matters. Resolutions are re-checked when kayfabe's WFI'd fence retires. The guest sees completion earlier, through the release it authored itself inside the work, and UVM can unmap and remap (invalidate, walk, rows change) before the pump re-checks. Those correct runs count as stale, and the gate requires stale_binds=0. In the other direction, an operand whose row is not there yet because another channel's walk has not landed fails at bind with VirtualUnresolved. That kills the channel instead of being counted, so the §11 decision-6 question is never measured.
findings.fix: Re-check against a per-mirror rows epoch that the walk increments. Count only changes whose walk was committed before the piece's own guest-visible release (record the epoch at bind and the walk sequence ordered before the fence). Separate 'unresolved, walk pending on this space' (stash and rebind) from 'unmapped' (refuse), and count each.

findings.issue: The shadow does not behave like T-mode when a segment contains its own invalidate. Shadow::observe decodes the whole segment at fetch time and binds every item against the current rows, including items after an Ir::Invalidate. T-mode binds those items only after the split's walk. So the CENSUS pass criteria (resolve_miss=0, would_refuse empty) can fail on correct UVM streams that write PTEs, invalidate and then use the new mapping in one push. They can also pass on rows T-mode would not see.
findings.fix: Stop binding at the first Ir::Invalidate in the shadow and keep the rest pending until the default path's split for that segment completes. Alternatively, count post-invalidate items in their own bucket and leave them out of the pass criteria.

findings.issue: On Hopper and later, T-mode turns a MEMORY_SCRUB launch into a ZERO fill (CONST_A=0, 1-byte DST_X) and drops the guest's pattern. UVM sends every 4 KiB-aligned physical-vidmem memset_1/4/8 through the scrubber, with the value in SET_REMAP_CONST_A/B (ogkm-580 uvm_hopper_ce.c:180-196, 232-258, 298-320). Page-table init uses non-zero clear_bits for PDE levels (uvm_mmu.c:475-498).
